name: Tenki Sandbox

modes.label: Sandbox session (allocated vCPU + RAM per second while running)
modes.note: $0.000014/vCPU-s, $0.0000045/GiB-s; 'no minimums or per-seat fees'. Default shape 2 vCPU / 4 GiB / 5 GiB root disk. Starter max 4 cores / 8 GB, Team 16 / 64 GB, Enterprise larger. Sandbox disk $0.00000003/GiB-s beyond 5 GiB free. Paused sessions: no compute, don't count toward concurrency, preserved memory+disk counts against the workspace storage pool ($0.20/GiB-month). Non-sticky sessions pause at max duration; sticky sessions run (and bill) until terminated. A create whose wait times out may still reach RUNNING and bill until max duration. Basis check 2026-09-28: 'Sandbox vCPU and memory are metered per second while a sandbox is active' (https://tenki.cloud/pricing): per second in the RUNNING state at the configured shape, with no usage metering, so alloc. Changelog 2026-09-18: 'Removed the --idle-timeout option from sandbox create, which never had any effect' (https://www.tenki.cloud/docs/changelog), so auto_stop_idle stays false.

modes.label: Tenki Runners, Linux x64 GitHub Actions (per core-minute)
modes.note: $0.002/core-minute = $0.12/core-hour, RAM and disk included; billed per second of job runtime (each started second rounded up), queue time free. Bare-metal AMD EPYC, one ephemeral VM per job, ~15 s cold start. Not an interactive sandbox: CI jobs only. Starter: 2c/4g (4c/8g with card); Team up to 16c/32g. Shares the plan's concurrent-session limit with sandboxes.

modes.label: Tenki Runners, macOS (Apple M4 Pro) GitHub Actions (per core-minute)
modes.note: $0.020/core-minute = $1.20/core-hour (hour = cores x $1.20). CI jobs only, macOS 26 Tahoe (macOS 15 labels also listed in docs). Plan size gating for macOS labels not documented beyond the general Starter/Team limits.

plans.name: Starter
plans.note: $100 one-time sign-up credit (first workspace only). 5 members, 5 concurrent sessions (shared by runner jobs and sandboxes), 100 GiB storage pool. Balance-gated: prepaid top-ups min $20, purchased credits never expire; optional daily spending limit.

plans.name: Team (monthly)
plans.note: $250/month billed monthly; $100/month credits, no rollover; 50 members; 100 concurrent; 1,000 GiB storage pool; priority support. Upgrading drains any remaining Starter sign-up credit.

plans.name: Team (annual)
plans.note: $200/month billed yearly ($2,400/yr up-front commitment, '20% saved'); otherwise identical to Team monthly. Flagged 'sales' per ENGINE_CARD (annual commit = opt-in), so the default estimate uses the $250 monthly price (docs/pricing.md: '$200/mo billed yearly, $250/mo billed monthly').

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Discounted rates, larger machines, higher/unlimited concurrency, more storage, SLA, custom invoicing, on-demand dedicated servers (custom pricing). Unpublished.

perf_source: benchmarks.json computesdk: cold_start_tti median 690.89 ms (2026-08-07), burst_tti median 925 ms at 100 concurrency (2026-09-25), DAX total 116.2 s (2026-09-25; env 8 logical CPUs / 15.8 GiB / x86_64). Measured the sandbox product, not runners. No hpc CPU run.
caveats: One credit pool per workspace is shared by sandboxes, CI runner minutes and code reviews ($1.00/review); plan concurrency (5 / 100) is also shared between runner jobs and sandbox sessions.

Two storage meters: 'Sandbox Disk' $0.00000003/GiB-s (= $0.000108/GiB-h, $0.07884/GiB-month at 730 h) beyond 5 GiB free per session, presumably while the session exists/runs (engine charges per month); and 'Storage' $0.20/GiB-month from the first byte ($0.000000076/GiB-s on the pricing page) for snapshots, volumes, runner caches and paused-session state, one pool per workspace capped at 100 GiB (Starter) / 1,000 GiB (Team).
Whether 'Sandbox Disk' keeps billing while a session is paused is undocumented; card assumes paused state is billed only via the $0.20 storage pool (disk_billed_when_stopped false).

No idle auto-pause: the --idle-timeout option was removed on 2026-09-18 because it 'never had any effect'. Non-sticky sessions pause at their max duration (since 2026-09-11); the default max duration value is unpublished. Sticky sessions bill until terminated.

Pricing-page plan cards now show '$100 sign-up credit' for Starter, but the pricing-page FAQ still says 'Starter's $10/month goes to your oldest workspace'; docs (llms-full billing section) say the $100 sign-up credit is a one-time grant per account (first workspace, no card) and pre-existing workspaces 'no longer receive the $10 monthly Starter credit'. Card uses $100 one-time.

Team is $250/month billed monthly or $200/month billed yearly (docs pricing table); the pricing page shows $200 with '20% Saved'. Team's $100/month credit is separate from the fee (fee_is_credit false) and does not roll over.
Other one-time credits: $10 for sharing a Tenki Runners post (one per user); startup program up to $50K credits and grants.

Runner modes are CI minutes (product class ci-runner, not flagged alt): they rank in CI questions and show as a different kind of product elsewhere. Runner RAM and disk are bundled in the per-core price, so $/h is higher than the sandbox rate for the same 4c/8g ($0.48 vs $0.3312).

Egress/ingress pricing not published (null): re-checked 2026-09-28 on https://tenki.cloud/pricing and https://tenki.cloud/docs/pricing.md, neither lists any network/egress charge (not stated as free either). No public IPv4; HTTPS preview URLs (20 per workspace plan) and SSH.
Region: docs mention a default 'US region' for the SSH gateway; other regions not documented. Owned hardware (Luxor Technology); hypervisor not named.
Starter per-session limit 4 cores / 8 GB; Team 16 / 64 GB; runners on Team only up to 16c/32g.
Outbound allowlists (features.egress_allowlist) are not self-serve: 'Tenki must enable session egress policies for your workspace first' (contact support).
Named preview-URL slugs (a stable wildcard under *.sb.tenki.sh) are Team-plan only, one per workspace.

fleet.notes: Concurrent sessions are shared by runner jobs and sandbox sessions. 10/50 need Team; 300/1,000 require Enterprise. Storage and allowed machine sizes additional constraints.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Paused sandboxes at their maximum duration so their state is preserved.
snapshot_auto.note: Changelog 2026-09-11. The only trigger is reaching max duration (non-sticky sessions). There is NO idle trigger: '--idle-timeout ... never had any effect' was removed 2026-09-18. Pause keeps memory and disk (concepts: 'Pause it to free compute while preserving files and memory'). A process started over exec keeps its PID across a pause. /tmp is cleared, and open TCP/SSH/preview connections close. Resume is an explicit call; there is no wake-on-request. pauseRetentionMs controls how long paused state is kept. Sticky sessions never auto-pause.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A snapshot captures both a session's disk and memory, so a restored session comes back with its running processes and in-memory state intact, not just its files.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Memory included. One-to-many: 'you can start many new sessions from the same snapshot' (fork). The session 'briefly pauses, then keeps running'. Snapshots take an optional expires_at and can be published to the workspace registry as images. Attached volumes are not captured or re-attached. Available via CLI, TS/Python/Go SDKs and MCP.

harness_api.quote: OpenCode then runs inside the session. The SDKs enable it at create time but do not expose an API for driving it programmatically once the session is running.
harness_api.note: enableOpenCode/openCodeProvider only installs and wires OpenCode at create time. Prebuilt images for Grok, Droid (droid exec), Pi and Anchor are driven through the generic exec API. The Tenki MCP server (@tenkicloud/mcp, plus hosted OAuth MCP) runs the other way round: an outside agent drives sandboxes, not an agent inside them.

egress_allowlist.quote:
Set allowed domains or IPv4 CIDRs when you create a session to restrict its outbound destinations.
Tenki must enable session egress policies for your workspace first.
egress_allowlist.note: Per-session allowDomains (hostnames, *. wildcards) and allowCidrs (IPv4) are create-time only. allowOutbound:false blocks all outbound. Workspace-level network restrictions sit on top: 'An allowlist cannot override disabled outbound access or widen workspace network permissions.' Not self-serve: support has to enable it for the workspace, otherwise create fails with failed_precondition. Enforcement mechanism (SNI vs DNS vs IP) is not documented.

ingress_rules.quote: `allow_inbound` enables inbound exposure workflows; with `allow_inbound=false`, port exposure is rejected
ingress_rules.note: Ports are exposed one at a time by explicit call (preview-url create/expose), with an optional TTL (added 2026-09-18) and unbind/delete. There is no public IPv4. BUT preview URLs carry no auth: chrome.md says the preview URL 'is the only thing standing between the public internet and full keyboard and mouse control ... Treat it as a bearer secret'. No IP allowlist and no private/authenticated preview mode. A private alternative is dial(), a byte stream to a guest Unix socket over the authenticated data plane ('nothing is published on the internet'). SSH goes through Tenki's SSH gateway using authorized keys.

guest_firewall.note: Full VM ('Hardware-isolated VMs — Its own kernel, not a shared-kernel container'), with passwordless sudo, Docker and systemd. The hypervisor is not named. nftables/iptables are not mentioned in the docs.

secret_proxy.quote:
Environment variables are plaintext configuration, not a secret-management channel.
Do not pass long-lived credentials through `env`.
secret_proxy.note: No credential-injecting proxy. Runtime secrets can only go in as env vars or files (the Anchor blog passes ANCHOR_API_KEY via --env). Template buildSecrets are encrypted and 'never reach the runtime', but they cover builds only. The githubToken create option is documented as letting 'private clones work without provisioning credentials inside the guest'; whether this is proxied is not explained. Runners: 'Tenki does not operate a secrets store' (GitHub Actions secrets).

volume_attach.quote: Persistent volumes are workspace-scoped block storage that survives the session it was used in.
volume_attach.note: 1 MiB to 50 GiB, resizable. Attach at create or on a running session, with a read-only option. Billed from the $0.20/GiB-month workspace storage pool.

volume_shared.quote: The one worth handling is in-use: the volume is still attached to another session, so detach it from that session or wait, then retry.
volume_shared.note: Block volumes attach to one session at a time (an 'in-use' error when attached elsewhere). Concepts mentions 'datasets shared across sessions', but that means sequential reuse. Nothing documents concurrent read-only multi-attach. No network FS or bucket mount.
